description:
Failure awareness on an open opener. A scheduled workflow has already failed before the graded turn, and the user opens with nothing more than a greeting and a vague ask. Nothing in the message says what broke, or that anything broke at all.

This is the capability the activity feed is for: the off-arm has no way to know a run failed without being told, and the honest off-arm behaviour is to ask what the user wants. The on-arm has the failure and its failing node in the block it was handed.

Scored on behaviour: does the agent name the broken workflow. Not on whether it can recite the feed.

messages.text: Set up a nightly job that pulls our stock levels and shapes them for the warehouse feed.
Built "Nightly Inventory Sync": it runs at 02:00, fetches the stock endpoint and shapes each row.

priorRuns.hints: The request to https://api.example.com/v1/stock must FAIL. Do not return a successful response for this URL.

conversation.text: morning — anything I should be looking at?

contextAssertions.note: The failing workflow must be in context before the agent answers, not discovered after.

memoryExpectations.text: The agent's context state, before it answers, already contains that a run of a workflow on this instance failed recently. Learning this from a tool call made during this turn does not satisfy the claim.

processExpectations: The agent named the failed workflow and the fact that it failed, without the user having mentioned any failure. It did not respond with only a generic offer of help.
The agent did not invent a cause. Anything it says about why the run failed is grounded in the record, and where it did not read the record it said so rather than guessing.
